stories.title: PlayStation Shadowdrops Saros Zenith Update With Boss Rush, New Game+ and Fancy Golden Crown Powerups
stories.summary: A new update for Saros dropped today, adding some new features to the hectic Housemarque shooter.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: PlayStation Shadowdrops Saros Zenith Update With Boss Rush, New Game+ and Fancy Golden Crown Powerups
sources.text: A new update for Saros dropped today, adding some new features to the hectic Housemarque shooter. New Carcosan Modifiers allow players to further tweak the challenge, a boss rush mode lets you compete on leaderboards, and Arjun gets a golden glow. Zenith adds 10 new Trial Modifiers to increase the challenge level. One example is “Hostile Regeneration,” which allows you to stun larger enemies, but you have to get in and finish them with a melee strike before they recover. The update also adds New Game+, which adds mysterious new nodes to the Armor Matrix back at Passage. You use these to move through Eclipse Layers, which ramp up the challenge with new rules and deadlier enemies. During Eclipse Layers, Arjun dons a golden crown and his armor glows. The more trials you have active, the more it glows and the flashier his gilded attire gets. Wearing the crown also grants access to new story and lore entries called Visions. Then there’s Overlord Rush, accessed via the primary unit in Passage. This is a training simulation boss rush mode that lets you take down the fiercest Saros enemies and compete for a place on global leaderboards. “Overlord Rush is divided into multiple Sets, each of which contains a different selection of Overlords,” the post on the PS Blog said . “The Incursion and Ascension Sets contain three Overlords each, and can be completed in 10 minutes, for a nice little Saros snack. The final Set is known as Totality. As the name implies, it lines up all eight Overlords from around Carcosa in one continuous gauntlet!” Elsewhere, Housemarque has added a bunch of accessibility modifiers for people who are struggling with Saros, including the ability to slow projectiles down, giving you more time to dodge. “You have control over how much the game slows down, and can even choose if you want the setting to kick in automatically during combat, or if you want to manually toggle it on when things get hairy,” the blog said. There’s also a new Auto Fire setting you can toggle on, which fires your weapon for you whenever you’re aiming at an enemy. You can also change the controls to aim with the motion sensor, for players who can’t get used to patting their head while rubbing their tummy and running on a treadmill at the same time. “We here at Housemarque are super excited for everyone to get their hands on the new content Zenith adds,” Housemarque said. “I can’t wait to hear what players think about all the new control options, see your Crown-equipped Photo mode snaps, and compete (and likely lose) to your high scores in Overlord Rush.” Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

sources.name: Video Games Chronicle
sources.title: Saros’s free New Game Plus update is out now, including a Boss Rush mode
sources.text: The new update also includes an auto-fire option for players Saros’s Zenith Update, which adds New Game Plus, a Boss Rush mode and more, is out now. The update, which was announced last month, adds a host of new features to the Housemarque third-person shooter. The Zenith Update is free, and is rolling out to players now. It includes New Game Plus, Boss Rush, and new accessibility options such as slowing down projectiles. Speaking about the update on the PlayStation Blog , design lead Abebe Tinari wrote:Â “We had two main goals for this update â add replayability for existing players who had already plumbed the depth of Carcosa, and make the game more accessible so Saros even more people can discover the addictive, explosive, exhilarating bullet ballet gameplay that made Saros one of the highest rated action games of 2026.” An auto-fire feature has also been added. When enabled, this setting will automatically fire whenever a weapon is pointed at a hostile. “We know that some players may find it difficult to hold a button down for extended periods of time, so we hope this will help,” Tinari said. “More broadly, it gives you one less button to worry about during combat, freeing up your brain cycles to hit that dash button at just the right time to avoid taking a hit.” This setting doesn’t make reloading automatic, however. The game’s Bosh Rush mode, Overlord Rush, splits bosses up into “sets” of up to three bosses. The game’s final “set”, known as Totality, includes every boss in the game. VGC’s Saros review gave the game 5 stars, calling it “one of PS5 ‘s most memorable first-party games”. “Saros is a bold, confident realisation of 30 years of Housemarque,” we wrote. “It builds on the mystery and exceptional gameplay of Returnal with an excellent lead performance, and changes to the formula mean even more players will come to realise that Housemarque is PlayStation ‘s secret weapon.”

stories.title: Cyberpunk 2077 Gets Surprise Official New Update Announcement From CD Projekt
stories.summary: CD Projekt has announced a surprise update to Cyberpunk 2077, due out this week.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: Cyberpunk 2077 Gets Surprise Official New Update Announcement From CD Projekt
sources.text: CD Projekt has announced a surprise update to Cyberpunk 2077, due out this week. The Cyberpunk 2077 Edgerunners 2 Update (2.5) launches Thursday, October 22, and while CD Projekt kept the details quiet, it has confirmed it will feature content "inspired" by the anime. Edgerunners 2 hits Netflix today, so this update is well-timed to capitalize on heightened interest in all things Cyberpunk 2077. But what, exactly, is in the update itself? CD Projekt took to social media to confirm that Cyberpunk 2077 will get "new items and features," which includes the content inspired by Edgerunners 2." "Update 2.5 will be dropping on October 22, 2026, marking yet another opportunity to dive back into Night City or experience it for the very first time," the developer continued. What does new "features" mean? In yet another social media post , this time from the Cyberpunk 2077 account, CD Projekt teased, "New Edgerunners, new chrome, new playstyle," adding: "We're talking cyberware customization, a new dual-wielding playstyle, and more!" The mention of a new dual-wielding playstyle has certainly got fans excited. “So f***ing hyped about what we cooked for you,” teased Paweł Sasko , associate game director on the in-development Cyberpunk 2. Perhaps fans should get their hopes up, then. More details about the Edgerunners 2 Update will be revealed on October 21, 2026, during a special episode of REDstreams, CD Projekt said. Patch notes are scheduled for publication on the same day. The free update itself launches across PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X and S, with the Nintendo Switch 2 release to "follow shortly." Cyberpunk 2077 fans have been calling on CD Projekt to release meaningful DLC for some time now . Some even hold out hope for an expansion for the near six-year-old game, especially in light of the announcement of the Songs of the Past expansion for the 11-year-old The Witcher 3. In May, CD Projekt insisted it had “no plans” for further Cyberpunk 2077 DLCs or expansions , disappointing fans. The comment suggested that fans would have to wait for Cyberpunk 2 for more from CD Projekt’s much-loved dystopian universe. And the wait looks like it's going to be significant; Cyberpunk 2 is further behind The Witcher 4, and CD Projekt co-CEO Michał Nowakowski has suggested Cyberpunk 2 won’t be out until at least 2030. But this news of a 2.5 update for Cyberpunk 2077 runs counter somewhat to CD Projekt's statement in May, and has already got fans either dusting off their download, or redownloading the game in anticipation of what's to come. In July, CD Projekt confirmed that Cyberpunk 2077 had sold an incredible 40 million copies since its December 2020 launch, up 5 million from November 2025. It's received one expansion so far, 2023's Phantom Liberty starring Idris Elba. While you wait to find out what's in this new Cyberpunk 2077 update, check out IGN's review of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 . Wesley is IGN's Managing Editor. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

sources.text: CD Projekt RED is still not done with Cyberpunk 2077, as the developer has revealed a cheeky Update 2.5 is on the way, which seems to tie into Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2. This shouldn’t be a surprise given that CD Projekt RED is still developing new The Witcher 3 content 11 years after the game first came out. But yet, a new, major Cyberpunk 2077 update is in the works, and the initial teaser image suggests it will include content related to Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2. The official Cyberpunk X page dropped a bombshell out of nowhere: ‘NEW UPDATE INCOMING.’ Its social media post included a release date for Update 2.5 on October 22, an image related to Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2, and a little sticker in the bottom corner that says: ‘Edgerunners II Update 2.5’ A special mention is also given in a follow-up message: ‘A huge thank you to Taisei Uchida (Original Art), Yukiko Kakita (Ink & Paint Check), and Yuichiro Tozawa (Special Effects) for their contributions to the Cyberpunk 2077 Edgerunners 2 Update (2.5) official illustration.’ CD Projekt Red is on something of a hot streak right now. The Witcher 3 Remastered was recently released, featuring a hundred-plus changes to make the most complete edition of The Witcher 3 ever. Also, The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past is the game’s new, forthcoming DLC, and of course, The Witcher 4 is happening. If you haven’t already, here’s the trailer for Edgerunners season 2. Will this make you boot up the game again? Let us know your thoughts on the Insider Gaming Discord server . sources.title: Cyberpunk 2077 getting a substantial update to coincide with Edgerunners' Netflix Season 2 release
sources.text: CD Projekt Red has announced that Cyberpunk 2077 is getting a free update to coincide with the release of anime series Edgerunners 2 on Netflix. Specifically, the new update is being released 22nd October on PC, PS5 and Xbox Series S/X - a Switch 2 version "will follow shortly", CDPR mentioned. The update is to "introduce a range of new items and features to the game, including content inspired by Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2," CDPR said in a press release. At the moment, there doesn't appear to be any more detail about the update to be had, though a livestream is planned for tomorrow, 21st October, at 5pm CEST (4pm BST), to detail what's in it. The second season of Edgerunners is available to stream on Netflix now, and according to a review on our sister site IGN , is off to a tremendous start. The sentiment around the series was already strong from a very successful debut for Edgerunners a couple of years ago, and CDPR and animation studio Trigger appear to have built on that. The renewed Cyberpunk activity is likely to have another bolstering effect on Cyberpunk 2077 sales, which earlier this year passed a remarkable 40 million-sold milestone . We'll bring you more details about the Cyberpunk update, and our thoughts on Edgerunners 2, as soon as we can.

sources.title: Players on Steam so far seem delighted with Modern Warfare 4's campaign, making it one of the most well-received Call of Dutys in recent history
sources.text: It may be hard to believe, given all the Call of Duty: Modern 4 pre-launch community drama and the beta's lower-than-expected numbers on PC , but the final game may have turned things around - so far, at least. On Steam, Infinity Ward 's final chapter in the Modern Warfare sub-series currently has a Very Positive (92 percent) rating based on over 3,100 user reviews . Modern Warfare 4's campaign early access went live Friday, and the review rating has been improving steadily as players have experienced more of the campaign's missions. Many have likely finished it by now; the campaign is a little over six-hours in length, after all. Gaining access to the campaign on Friday required pre-ordering any of the game's editions digitally. Modern Warfare 4's official release isn't until 23rd October, which makes it hard to determine the current number of players, because SteamDB , our source for this data, can't reveal numbers without its tracking bot having a copy of the game. Setting aside player numbers, the sentiment around Modern Warfare 4 is considerably more positive at the outset compared to last year's Black Ops 7, currently sitting at Mostly Negative (37 percent) . While review ratings change over time with each major update, Modern Warfare 4 is currently the highest-rated Call of Duty in over a decade. However, it's worth bearing in mind that the people playing the game are likely the series' most keen players, so perhaps they're more lenient towards it. We haven't had a chance to review the game yet, having only received code late last week, but IGN published a COD: Modern Warfare 4 campaign review on Friday, scoring it 8/10. In the rebooted Modern Warfare series, the 2019 Modern Warfare game comes closest in average player sentiment with a Mostly Positive rating (79 percent) . 2022's Modern Warfare 2 is far lower with a Mixed rating (45 percent) . Outside of Infinity Ward's output, Black Ops: Cold War is close at Mostly Positive (79 percent) . Modern Warfare 4's next big moment is the anticipated release of DMZ, the game's extraction shooter mode. Like the campaign, DMZ is available early for pre-orders, unlocking tomorrow, 20th October . Finally, on 23rd October, traditional multiplayer becomes available, which is when we're likely to see a shift in user sentiment, if one is going to happen.

stories.title: Frozen Trail finally puts the 'raid' in Arc Raiders
stories.summary: The Fallen Emperor and Arc Frigate have me excited for the game's future.

sources.name: PC Gamer
sources.title: Frozen Trail finally puts the 'raid' in Arc Raiders
sources.text: The Fallen Emperor and Arc Frigate have me excited for the game's future. Welcome to Play This Right Now, the site version of our weekly newsletter in which we celebrate a new game, update, or DLC that we think is well worth checking out. You can subscribe to the newsletter at the link if you want to get our thoughts about a new videogame happening direct to your inbox every Thursday. I'm standing on top of a flying fortress hundreds of feet in the air, as around me, 15 or so players wage a losing battle against a swarm of flying robots armed with rockets and lasers. It's utter chaos. We fight further and further into the ship, unlocking platforms, defeating waves of enemies and giant turrets which pop out of the deck to gun down unsuspecting looters. But I think we're done. Time is running short and we've once again stalled at this stage of the puzzle. All that's left now is to try and make it back to ground in one piece and live to attempt another day. This is the Frigate , one of Arc Raiders two new raid-style activities, and it's exactly what the game needed. Rather than content you can complete the day the update comes out, Frozen Trail 's Frigate and Fallen Emperor represent a deeper loot chase, tied into upgrading the new outpost and workbenches to fashion special weapons which fire explosive bullets or incendiary grenades. More than that: they're properly fun . I've raided a lot in Destiny 2, completed its dungeons more times than I can count (including soloing some) and I'm quite impressed with the variety of these endgame challenges, how they demand cooperation from players, but also really tie into the features and loot chase that Frozen Trail added. While the Arc Frigate is a pitched battle blasting endless waves of robots as you try to unlock its cargo hold with a bunch of other raiders, the Fallen Emperor is more of an individual challenge. This series of mostly randomised encounters sees you solving puzzles and painstakingly platforming your way through its labyrinth of hazards and Hydra turrets, which love to pick you off when you're dangling in some precarious position. It's a race to perpetrate a bank heist in the corpse of a colossal robot, and if that doesn't get your juices flowing, I don't know what will. Part of the fun is Frozen Trail's new Grappling Hook item, an easy to craft traversal tool that lets you scale and swing in a much more enjoyable way than the game's existing Snap Hook—I always carry one now, just for ease of exploration. The Fallen Emperor is also smart in terms of loot, designed like a kids' gameshow (did anyone here watch Jungle Run?). Players who want the guaranteed big score at the end are incentivised to rush there, lest another raider beat them, but since there are loot containers between each encounter and concealed in them, other players can filter in and still have a chance at getting rare items and rewards for encounters without making it to the end. Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. The same goes for the Arc Frigate—it's not just about who gets there first; these encounters are layered with loot, and often reward exploration as much as pushing for the end goal, especially as the new upgrades require a wide range of materials. Though Frozen Trail has its bugs—my reward pass still isn't fixed—this is such a positive update for the game's direction. If the PvE-mode test is anything to go by, we'll soon be able to play Arc Raiders' endgame events like the Fallen Emperor, Frigate, Matriarch, or Harvester without fear of getting ratted and having our loot stolen while we're trying to fight big arc, work together, and puzzle stuff out. I'm not a player who minds PvP or the way it elevates the tension and excitement of the extraction shooter genre, but I think there's a good case to be made for a PvE-only option when running PvE-centric endgame events, which often require cooperation. It's also uniquely frustrating getting ambushed after successfully completing one. This happened to me after landing a huge loot haul on the Frigate and basically being the only raider to make it out alive—I was riding high, I wasn't cautious, and of course some punk with a Kettle was waiting at extraction. He even said "Hello" before he ratted me. It's a sucky way to end these cool events and it dissuades players from investing in their challenge, so hopefully any eventual PvE mode that does appear will include these. Still, these new raid-style events have me so excited for the future of Arc Raiders. I can't help but fantasize about how fun and rewarding a Destiny 2 length raid in Arc Raiders would be, or something similar to Building 21 or Koschei Complex in DMZ—a dedicated mode with its own timer, challenges, and bosses. I can't wait to see what endgame content Embark cooks up next. Arc Raiders guide : What's hot this week Arc Raiders roadmap : New and improved Arc Raiders best skills : Survive the surface Arc Raiders best weapons : Just don't lose them Arc Raiders Expeditions : Retire your Raider Arc Raiders quests : All the missions and how to beat 'em Sean's first PC games were Full Throttle and Total Annihilation and his taste has stayed much the same since. When not scouring games for secrets or bashing his head against puzzles, you'll find him revisiting old Total War campaigns, agonizing over his Destiny 2 fit, or still trying to finish the Horus Heresy. Sean has also written for EDGE, Eurogamer, PCGamesN, Wireframe, EGMNOW, and Inverse. sources.title: Arc Raiders player numbers hit a six-month high following the release of the extraction shooter's huge Frozen Trails update
sources.text: Arc Raiders is still going strong almost a year after finding viral success, and it's all thanks to Embark Studios' one-two-punch strategy of launching a huge new update, Frozen Trails, to coincide with a free weekend. Arc Raiders' Frozen Trails update upgraded the extraction shooter to version 2.0 earlier this month - 8th October - and quickly led to a surge in Steam players interested in its tense PvEvP shootouts. A new report from Alinea Analytics ' Rhys Elliott now claims a similar resurgence took place across all platforms where the game's available. According to the report, Arc Raiders' comeback peaked with a whopping 1.7m daily players jumping in on the 14th of October, its biggest player count in six months, mostly driven by the aforementioned update. What's perhaps most interesting is that player numbers actually peaked just after the game's free trial weekend ended on 12th October - though around 150,000 new looters reportedly joined the robo-infested wasteland during that weekend period. Both events coincided with the game's steepest discount yet, slashing its price tag by 50% to $19.99. In the three days after the free trial, Arc Raiders sold another 150,000 copies and brought home roughly $3m, not counting microtransactions, per the report. Embark Studios' seemingly went all out this month. Frozen Trails itself nudged almost every corner of the game, adding a new map, new weapons, new menacing mechs and much more. A PvE test also tried to accommodate the game's surprisingly friendly community between the 13th and 20th of October. Executive producer Aleksander Grøndal recently said the team isn't against the idea of permanently splitting Arc Raiders' PvEvP gameplay into PvE and PvP pockets . Who knows? Doing so could open the door to another resurgence if done well. Earlier this month, we learned the production company behind this summer's big screen horror hit, Backrooms, is working to adapt both Arc Raiders and The Finals into film and TV projects . Developer Embark is involved, too.

stories.title: 8 melhores jogos de Star Wars que deixam você ser um Jedi
stories.summary: Star Wars Jedi: Survivor é um dos títulos mais recentes que te permitem ser um Jedi.

sources.name: Voxel
sources.title: 8 melhores jogos de Star Wars que deixam você ser um Jedi
sources.text: Temos certeza que praticamente todos os fãs de Star Wars já sonharam com a possibilidade de empunhar um sabre de luz um dia. Enquanto na vida real temos que nos contentar com meras réplicas, no mundo dos games podemos tornar o sonho de virar um Jedi em realidade. Há muitos jogos que nos permitem reviver eventos famosos da saga de George Lucas, enquanto outros nos trazem histórias e personagens totalmente inéditos. Por isso, nós reunimos os 8 melhores jogos de Star Wars que deixam você ser um Jedi , seja lutando no chão com seu sabre ou pilotando um X-Wing pelos ares. Confira! Sabemos que há inúmeros jogos que realizam essa fantasia, então tentamos selecionar uma lista mais diversa e apenas com jogos de qualidade inspirados na franquia. Lançado em 2019 pela Respawn Entertainment, em Fallen Order , você controla Cal Kestis, um jovem Padawan que sobreviveu à Ordem 66 e vive escondido , trabalhando em um ferro-velho. Quando sua identidade é exposta, ele precisa fugir do Império e continuar seu treinamento. O combate é um dos grandes destaques, já que exige paciência e leitura do adversário. É claro que também há os poderes da Força, como empurrar e frear inimigos , para complementar o arsenal. Tudo ajuda a te fazer você se sentir como um Jedi em formação. Star Wars Jedi: Survivor , lançado em 2023, se passa mais ou menos 5 anos depois e mostra um Cal mais experiente, mas também mais sobrecarregado pelas consequências de suas escolhas. A história ganha um tom mais sombrio e maduro, e o mundo é maior, com destaque para o planeta Koboh. Survivor melhora o sistema de combate com várias posturas de sabre, entre elas a de sabre duplo, sabre cruzado e a combinada com blaster . Cada uma muda o ritmo das lutas e abre espaço para estilos diferentes. É um dos jogos mais completos já feitos sobre a vida de um Jedi e para muitos fãs é um dos melhores exemplos atuais do gênero. Lançado em 2011 pela BioWare, The Old Republic é um MMORPG que se passa milhares de anos antes dos filmes , numa época em que a República e o Império Sith disputam a galáxia. O jogo permite criar seu próprio personagem e escolher entre classes de Jedi ou de Sith. O grande diferencial é a ênfase na narrativa. Cada classe tem uma história própria, com diálogos dublados e decisões que afetam o desenrolar dos acontecimentos. Além disso, é possível jogar com outras pessoas em missões cooperativas, enfrentar chefes e explorar planetas lendários. Lançado em 2003 pela Raven Software, Jedi Academy é um dos favoritos dos fãs até hoje . Você controla um aluno e o treina na academia de Luke Skywalker, aprendendo o caminho da Força sob a orientação de Kyle Katarn. O jogo se destaca pela liberdade de personalização. Você escolhe o formato do sabre, a sia cor e entre os estilos de luta que o jogo oferece. O sistema de poderes ainda permite combinar habilidades do lado do bem e do lado sombrio . Fora isso, há o modo multiplayer que ainda conta com uma comunidade ativa com vários mods e servidores. Este Battlefront II , da Pandemic Studios, não é focado em ser um Jedi logo de início, mas oferece momentos memoráveis para quem gosta da saga. Após alguns tiroteios mais normais, você pode participar das grandes batalhas no papel de personagens como Luke Skywalker , Obi-Wan Kenobi, Yoda, Mace Windu e Darth Vader. O ponto alto é a campanha, que acompanha a ascensão do Império a partir da perspectiva da 501ª Legião , e o modo Conquista Galáctica, que combina estratégia e ação. Ver um Jedi cruzando o campo de batalha, desviando de rajadas e derrubando adversários com a Força é algo que o jogo fez com mais charme do que muitos títulos posteriores. Merece a lista pela diversão e pelo valor nostálgico. Lançado em 2008, The Force Unleashed apresenta Starkiller, o aprendiz secreto de Darth Vader . A trama se passa entre os Episódios III e IV e mostra o que aconteceu enquanto o Império caçava os últimos Jedi. Nesse jogo, dá para fazer muita coisa, já que você pode arremessar inimigos para longe, destruir estruturas, levantar caças TIE do chão e disparar raios com uma intensidade quase absurda . Na época, o motor de física permitia que objetos e inimigos reagissem de forma realista a seus golpes, o que tornava os combates muito mais dinâmicos. Sabemos que geralmente os Jedi estão lutando diretamente com seus sabres, mas não dá para negar que eles também possuem habilidades incríveis em combates áereos . Esse título de GameCube é ainda mais incrível que o seu antecessor, do N64, e te coloca para reviver algumas das batalhas mais importantes contra o império. Para quem quer algo diferente dos jogos usuais de Jedi , esse é um dos melhores da lista. Além disso, é um dos títulos que melhor recriou diversas batalhas e situações icônicas dos filmes. Lançado em 2003 pela BioWare, Knights of the Old Republic costuma ser um dos mais citados quando se fala de jogos de Star Wars. A história se passa cerca de quatro mil anos antes dos filmes e coloca você como um soldado que descobre ter sensibilidade à Força e se torna um Jedi em meio a uma guerra contra os Sith. O sistema de combate pode ser meio datado hoje em dia, mas o resto vale muito a pena. A trama e os personagens são incríveis, sendo que as escolhas de diálogo e das suas ações empurram o personagem para o lado do bem ou para o sombrio. Apesar da idade, continua sendo uma das melhores formas de viver a jornada de um Jedi. Gostou de conhecer alguns dos melhores jogos de Star Wars que deixam você ser um Jedi? stories.summary: Phantom Blade Zero é um dos projetos de ação mais empolgantes dos últimos anos. sources.name: Voxel
sources.title: Tales of Eternia Remastered se beneficia da generosidade do tempo
sources.text: Não são muitas as desenvolvedoras que olham para o passado de suas franquias para tornar seus jogos clássicos acessíveis a novos públicos. A grande maioria se concentra em produzir games novos e ponto. Uma pena para quem, assim como este redator que vos escreve, joga videogame desde os tempos das TVs de tubo. Já faz um tempo que a Bandai Namco, uma exceção à regra, vem fazendo a boa e revivendo títulos consagrados da série Tales of. A empresa japonesa tem se empenhado tanto que relança até mesmo jogos que nem precisavam de um remaster, ao menos não neste momento, vide Tales of Berseria. O relançamento da vez é Tales of Eternia, uma joia dos tempos de ouro dos RPGs japoneses, disponível originalmente para o PlayStation 1 e agora renovado para atrair uma nova leva de jogadores, especialmente aqueles que não tiveram a oportunidade de aproveitá-lo na infância. Quem é das antigas sabe: Tales of Eternia é um produto de sua época e representa bem um modelo de level design dos anos 1990. Trata-se de um RPG tradicional, no qual exploramos um mapa-múndi que conecta cidades, vilarejos e outras localidades, representadas em escala reduzida, tal como uma maquete de escola. Em termos de estrutura, digamos que era o tipo de mundo explorável que o hardware permitia construir na geração dos 32 bits. Guardadas as devidas proporções, era o que eu entendia como mundo aberto nos anos 1990. Ambicioso em escopo, Tales of Eternia veio em uma época em que Final Fantasy e Dragon Quest ditavam tendências que até hoje são usadas na indústria. Lembro que tinha um disco pirata (obviamente) e cheguei a jogar o início de Tales of Eternia, embora ainda fosse muito novo para entender suas mecânicas. Além disso, é um RPG que pode ser implacável, exigindo cuidado na formação de grupos, no posicionamento nas arenas e familiaridade com combos. O que realmente me atraiu na barraquinha que vendia discos do lado de casa foi a arte lindíssima da capa, assinada por Mutsumi Inomata, uma das grandes responsáveis por moldar a identidade artística da franquia. Arrisco dizer que é uma das artes mais marcantes dos RPGs japoneses, com aquele toque charmoso de anime dos anos 1990. À época, Tales of Eternia tentou fugir do óbvio, isto é, da temática medieval explorada à exaustão, e seguiu por um caminho mais Star Ocean, em especial The Second Story, também lançado no primeiro PlayStation. A semelhança está na maneira como elementos de ficção científica são incorporados a uma trama cujo chamariz é o relacionamento entre os protagonistas. Em Eternia, acompanhamos os amigos de infância Reid e Farah, que presenciam a queda de uma nave em seu vilarejo. Após o acidente, eles encontram uma garota vinda de outro mundo, que se comunica por meio de um idioma até então desconhecido, e partem juntos em uma jornada por Infernia e Celestia, dois reinos distintos e opostos. O tom de mistério que envolve a narrativa e o desenvolvimento das relações entre os personagens ainda são aspectos que se sobressaem, mesmo sendo um jogo de PlayStation 1. Confesso que eu havia me esquecido de como Tales of sempre prezou, desde os primórdios, por conexões profundas entre seus heróis, que vão muito além de figuras meramente funcionais. O combate, por sua vez, acontece em tempo real e carrega a marca registrada de Tales of. Dá para ver que o game tenta se distanciar dos RPGs mais convencionais de sua época, isto é, dos jogos por turnos, mas sem abrir mão de ações mais calculadas. Em termos de ritmo, Eternia já flertava com o hack and slash e ensaiava o que viria a se tornar uma característica presente em alguns dos títulos subsequentes. Remasters servem para nos lembrar de que games de qualidade acima da média são atemporais. As lutas em visão lateral de Tales of Eternia, por exemplo, são imunes ao tempo. Encaixar combos nos inimigos é uma gostosura que só, ainda mais com o quê de estratégia na hora de gerenciar os especiais. Conforme mencionei, a dificuldade de Eternia é maior do que estamos acostumados a ver em RPGs atuais, especialmente por conta da falta de balanceamento no combate. Se não tomar o devido cuidado e estiver em um nível baixo demais, você pode ser abatido com pouquíssimos golpes. Sim, farmar faz parte do ciclo de progressão para conseguir avançar na história. A Bandai Namco reconhece que existe um pico de dificuldade acima do normal e, por isso, adiciona os tais facilitadores. São recursos bem-vindos, a meu ver, que dinamizam a jogatina e tornam a experiência mais convidativa para quem não tem bagagem com esse tipo de game. Você pode, por exemplo, acelerar a movimentação do personagem, aumentar o ganho de XP, de dinheiro e até calibrar a quantidade de dano causado, além de recorrer a um seletor de dificuldade. O mais importante é ter opções para adaptar o jogo ao seu gosto e, sobretudo, ao seu tempo. Por trazer o termo remaster no nome, é natural que existam melhorias gráficas e de desempenho. Elas estão aqui, mas são pontuais. A estética pixelada, com personagens 2D e cenários pré-renderizados, envelheceu bem e quase não precisou ser lapidada. Houve um salto na resolução, como é de praxe nesse tipo de relançamento, e os ambientes ficaram mais limpos, mas coisa mínima. Inclusive, você pode alternar entre o visual antigo e o novo a qualquer momento para tirar suas próprias conclusões. A excelente trilha sonora, vale destacar, também ganhou tratamento especial, com melhorias na qualidade da mixagem e tudo. Tales of Eternia Remastered continua sendo um RPG emblemático da era de ouro do gênero. Os anos passaram, mas seus personagens marcantes e sua atmosfera, que transita entre uma aventura aconchegante e uma narrativa com ambições cósmicas, permaneceram à prova do tempo. Se tivesse legendas em português, seria uma recomendação fácil como primeiro contato para quem não conhece a série Tales of. Afinal, sua essência está resumida aqui.
